mechanism_narrative: GDP growth indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment above 5% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: If unemployment exceeds 5% but S&P 500 returns remain positive.

mechanism_narrative: When employment increases and unemployment decreases, it signals a strong economy, boosting S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: If employment rises and unemployment drops but S&P 500 returns are not positive.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening cycle, higher FEDFUNDS indicates tighter monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rise but S&P 500 returns do not decline.

mechanism_narrative: High CPI inflation may lead to monetary policy tightening, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns in 5 days.
failure_condition: If CPI is high but S&P 500 returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: Strong housing starts indicate economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If housing starts exceed 1200 but S&P 500 returns do not rise.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production and retail sales signal economic growth, boosting S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: If both indicators rise but S&P 500 returns are not positive.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment in late-cycle may lead to tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If unemployment is low but S&P 500 returns do not decline.
